title: 1957 AHSME Problem 46
statement: Two perpendicular chords intersect in a circle. The segments of one chord are \(3\) and \(4;\) the segments of the other are \(6\) and \(2.\) Then the diameter of the circle is:

solutions.text:
Place the intersection at \((0,0)\) with endpoints \((-3,0),\) \((4,0),\) \((0,-2),\) and \((0,6).\) The perpendicular bisectors of the chords are \(x=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y=2,\) so the center is \((\frac{1}{2},2).\) Using the endpoint \((4,0),\) \[ \begin{aligned} r^2 &=\left(4-\frac12\right)^2+(0-2)^2\\ &=\frac{65}{4}. \end{aligned} \] Therefore the diameter is \(2r=\sqrt{65}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Place the chord intersection at the origin and the perpendicular chords on the coordinate axes
The circle’s center lies on both chord perpendicular bisectors
